title: Test CCP2 sync loss and root transitions end to end
description:
Scope: one synchronization scenario module under /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/python/tests/sim/scenarios/, exercising actual Python/Rust/C receive/timer/scheduler paths through the native-peer harness. Inject independently signed data, malformed/stale/retired-root beacons, invalid provenance and valid recovery objects with exact clock events. Compare actual state and TX behavior to the frozen CCP2 synchronization oracle. Do not directly call a test-local FSM or count generic authentication as beacon qualification.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Drive events through the same receive/timer path used by production, keeping clock and signature inputs independent from expected transitions. Reuse existing synchronization primitives without rewriting them inside tests.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly three missed qualified beacon opportunities stop scheduled TX and exactly three consecutive valid recovery beacons restore it under the adopted time policy. Ordinary signed data cannot refresh the timer; invalid/stale/retired-root events cannot recover or mutate adopted state. Interrupted recovery, epoch-floor failure, root/generation transition and SFN wrap have the independently specified outcomes at the real radio boundary. Commands and event artifacts are reproducible and hardware-free.
